text:
incident-bot: ALERT: prod /v1/generate p95 latency spiking above 1.2s; queue depth increasing; impacted regions: us-east-1, eu-west-1. Auto-scaling not keeping up. Paging on-call: @maya

maya: taking it — paging @devon and @priya. I’m on call for infra today.

devon: seeing large continuous batching window growth, lots of small requests pinned up. p50 ok, p95 and p99 bad. Could be request shape shift (many short prompts).

priya: routing shows burst of streaming chat sessions from a customer in eu-west — likely high concurrency causing many tiny batches.

maya: quick customer-impact check: do we have any elevated error rates?

sam: no spike in 5xxs, just token-slowing. Traces show long tail at the batching queue waiting for batch fill timeout.

maya: ok mitigation plan (live): 1) temporarily increase batching window to favor throughput (sacrifice latency) 2) add soft rate-limit for free-tier and guests 3) disable non-essential post-processing that adds latency 4) hotfix dashboard to monitor per-customer queue length. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

devon: agreed. I’ll push a conservative change to continuous batching config to increase max_wait_ms from 20 -> 60 and bump max_batch_size  to 1024 -> 2048 on the heavyweight pool. That should drain queues faster.

priya: please can we also shape traffic by lowering burst token allowance for anonymous keys? We have a quick policy we can toggle.

maya: @ops-bot flip policy "guest-rate-limit" -> 10rps (was 50rps) in prod us-east-1 and eu-west-1.

ops-bot: applying policy change: guest-rate-limit -> 10rps for tags: {env:prod, tier:guest} ... DONE.

devon: deploying batching config change to canary hosts (2/20) now. Patch: ```
# continuous batching config
continuous_batching:
  max_wait_ms: 60
  max_batch_size: 2048
  max_concurrency: 128
  priority_threshold: 0.7
```

priya: rolling canary. If canary looks good for 2 minutes, push to 50% then all. Also prepare rollback: set max_wait_ms back to 20 and max_batch_size 1024.

maya: customer comms: product-led customers might see increased single-request latency but fewer timeouts. Flagging support to expect latency tickets. @sam can you post a quick note to #support?

sam: will do. Posting note with guidance to explain tradeoff and that this is temporary mitigation.

devon: canary metrics: queue depth dropped 40% on canary hosts, p95 on canary reduced from 1250ms -> 900ms (interesting, maybe filling bigger batches improved kernel throughput). However initial single-request latency increased ~120ms. No increase in errors.

priya: pushing to 50% now. Monitoring CPU/GPU saturation.

maya: good. Also enable temporary quota throttle for top noisy API keys to protect tail. Script to add keys to "burst_protect" list: ```
for key in $(cat noisy_keys.txt); do
  ./policyctl add throttle $key --rps 5 --duration 15m
done
```

ops-bot: throttle applied to 7 API keys, duration 15m.

elliot: looking at logs — we also have a KV cache prefetch job that runs every minute and coincides with the burst, adding occasional contentions. Can we disable prefetch temporarily?

maya: yes — disable prefetch on prod at 2:20. @devon can you remove the cron?

devon: disabled prefetch cron on prod. Confirmed no new prefetch logs.

priya: 50% rollout looks healthy: global p95 down 30%, queue lengths stable. But memory pressure slightly higher due to larger batch KV caching. Watching.

maya: OK hold at 50% while we observe for 20m. Support/CS notified.

[10 minutes pass]

ops-bot: Canary -> 50% -> 100% rollout started.

devon: full rollout complete. Metrics: p95 back to 700-900ms in affected regions, throughput up ~1.6x. Single-request tail increased median by ~80-150ms but error rate unchanged.

maya: mitigation summary: continuous batching tuned (max_wait_ms 60, max_batch_size 2048), guest rate-limit reduced (50->10rps), throttles applied to noisy keys, KV prefetch disabled, temporary post-processing offload.

priya: we should schedule a post-incident action: add an adaptive batching policy that adjusts max_wait_ms based on queue depth and recent interarrival times. Also add per-customer queue length alerts.

sam: noted — filing an RCA ticket and an action item for adaptive batching and per-key rate limits.

maya: handing back to normal rotation. If any regression, ping this thread. Thanks everyone :rocket:
